stem: Why is aPTT followed during a therapeutic continuous IV unfractionated heparin infusion?

options.A: To guide heparin dose adjustment using coagulation-test response
options.B: To measure the client’s serum potassium concentration
options.D: To replace all platelet-count monitoring during heparin therapy

rationale: The current heparin label directs clinicians to adjust dosage according to coagulation-test results and to follow aPTT during continuous IV infusion, initially about every 4 hours and then at appropriate intervals.
educational_objective: Relate aPTT monitoring to response-based dose adjustment during therapeutic IV unfractionated heparin therapy.
source_version_date: Current DailyMed Version 20 published July 6, 2026; prescribing information revised January 2025
source_locator: Dosage and Administration, Section 2.3 > Laboratory Monitoring for Efficacy and Safety
source_claim_supported: Heparin dosage is adjusted according to coagulation tests; aPTT is followed during continuous IV infusion.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
correction_summary: Avoided calling aPTT the only possible heparin-monitoring method and used the exact current label dose-adjustment role.
audit_findings: A matches the label. B and C measure unrelated variables; D is false because platelet counts remain recommended. No second answer remains.
